instructions: The night before, or at least 2 hours ahead: juice 1 of the lemons into a large bowl. That should be about 3 tbsp. Mince 2 of the garlic cloves and add them to the bowl with 1/4 cup of the Greek yogurt, the 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tbsp olive oil, the 1 tbsp oregano, 3/4 tsp of the salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper. Stir it until it's smooth.
Add the 1.5 lbs chicken thighs and turn them over in the marinade until every piece is coated. Cover the bowl and put it in the fridge.
On the night, make the tzatziki first. Halve 2 of the cucumbers lengthwise, scrape out the seeds with a teaspoon, and grate them on the large holes of a box grater.
Squeeze the grated cucumber a handful at a time in a clean kitchen towel until no more water comes out. Squeeze hard, or the tzatziki will be runny.

Grate the last garlic clove into a bowl. Add the squeezed cucumber, the remaining 1 1/4 cups Greek yogurt, 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp juice from the second lemon and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Stir it together and put it in the fridge for at least 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, dice the 3 tomatoes and the other 2 cucumbers. Finely chop half the red onion and chop 1/4 cup of the parsley. Toss them together in a bowl with the last 1/4 tsp salt.

Heat a large skillet or grill pan over medium-high heat with the last 1 tbsp olive oil until it shimmers. Lift half the chicken out of the marinade, let the extra drip off, and lay it in the pan in one layer.

Leave it alone for 4 to 5 minutes, until the underside is golden with dark spots and lets go of the pan. Flip the pieces and cook the other side for 4 to 5 minutes. You're cooking it to 175°F, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when there's no pink left and the juices run clear.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and cook the second half the same way. Throw away the leftover marinade. Cover the plate loosely with foil and let the chicken rest for 5 minutes.
While it rests, wipe out the pan and warm the 4 pitas in it over medium heat, about 30 seconds on each side, until they're soft and warm.
Slice the chicken into strips. Taste a piece. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
Serve the chicken in the warm pitas with the tomato salad and the tzatziki.
advance_prep_notes: Marinate the chicken at least 2 hours ahead, ideally the night before.
method_notes: Both versions marinate boneless thighs in Greek yogurt, lemon, garlic and dried oregano, then wrap the sliced chicken in warm pita with a cucumber tzatziki and fresh vegetables. RecipeTin Eats (the lead) adds a splash of vinegar, marinates 2 to 12 hours and cooks the thighs fast in a hot pan, with a chopped tomato, cucumber and onion salad; Kristine's Kitchen adds cumin and coriander, bakes the thighs at 425°F and uses lettuce and dill. This follows the lead at 4 servings, cooked in two batches so the chicken browns, and gives the thighs 4 to 5 minutes a side since thighs here are usually thicker than the lead's.
